strengths: Addresses well-motivated limitations of CholecT50 with clear evidence: missing spatial annotations, inconsistent temporal boundaries, and single-source bias
Rigorous annotation methodology with >50 contributors, multiple verification phases, and clinically-grounded temporal boundary definitions (continuous vs. momentary actions)
Multi-source data from three institutions reduces single-source bias and reflects real-world variability in instruments and surgical strategies
Increased task complexity meaningfully reflects real-world surgical environments: up to 7 concurrent triplets/frame vs. CholecT50 max 3, demonstrating clinical relevance
Comprehensive evaluation with 10+ baseline methods showing clear performance gap between weak supervision (Tripnet-Det/RDV-Det: <2% mAP) and full supervision (best methods: 35% mAP)
Novel Triplet Perspective tracking annotation extends beyond standard instrument-only tracking to capture semantic evolution of surgical actions
Proper ethical considerations including IRB approval, data anonymization, informed consent, and non-commercial licensing
weaknesses: Modest absolute performance despite full supervision (F1: 31.26%, Precision/Recall: ~35%) remains far below clinical deployment thresholds, raising concerns about fundamental task solvability versus dataset difficulty
Limited algorithmic novelty: YOLO-Triplet is straightforward combination of YOLOv12 + ResNet18 + attention; primarily a data contribution with minimal methodological innovation
Insufficient scale by modern standards: only 21 videos total (14 for training) and 165K instances heavily dependent on per-video statistics; comparable datasets typically contain hundreds of videos
Long-tail distribution explicitly acknowledged but unaddressed: no proposed handling strategies, loss weighting, or sampling methods provided despite 100+ categories occurring <100 times

Missing inter-annotator agreement statistics: no Cohen's/Fleiss' kappa, reliability metrics, or formal documentation of disagreement resolution procedures; 'extremely close to' contact remains subjective
Limited cross-source generalization validation: no systematic cross-institution evaluation (train on [Our+PSI-AVA] → test on ESAD) despite multi-source advantage claims
Scope narrowly limited to single surgical procedure (robot-assisted prostatectomy only) with questionable generalization to other surgical specialties or open procedures
No systematic ablation studies demonstrating bounding box annotation value or temporal boundary impact; limited analysis of which dataset characteristics drive performance gaps

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine limitations in CholecT50 (lack of bounding boxes, unclear temporal boundaries, single institution)
Rigorous annotation process with 50+ contributors including practicing surgeons, multiple verification rounds, and proper IRB oversight
Comprehensive dataset characterization with detailed statistics, complexity analysis, and clear comparison with CholecT50 demonstrating higher surgical complexity
Extensive empirical evaluation of 12+ detection methods with both mAP and Precision-Recall metrics, providing good architectural insights
Multi-source dataset integration combining in-house, PSI-AVA, and ESAD data to reduce single-source bias
Novel contribution of Triplet Perspective for surgical tracking that extends beyond instrument-only approaches
Commitment to reproducibility with promised code and dataset release under open licensing
weaknesses: No inter-annotator agreement metrics provided, critical omission for a dataset paper; quality validation relies only on majority voting without reporting disagreement frequency or magnitude

Unsatisfactory absolute performance (best F1-score 31.26%, mAP@95 33.81%) with authors acknowledging results are 'significantly below threshold for reliable clinical deployment', raising concerns about annotation quality or task feasibility

Limited technical novelty - purely a dataset paper with no novel algorithmic contributions; proposed YOLO-Triplet baseline is straightforward and doesn't convincingly outperform standard YOLO variants, questioning whether sophisticated relation modeling is needed

No generalization validation despite claims that multi-source data helps; missing cross-dataset evaluation (ProstaTD→CholecT50 transfer) and no evidence that models trained on ProstaTD generalize better than CholecT50-trained ones
Limited scope with only one surgical procedure type and 21 total videos, reducing generalizability claims
Missing critical ablations: no ablation on impact of bounding boxes vs. class labels, no comparison on temporal boundary strictness, no error analysis by category
Pronounced long-tail distribution with 40+ categories having <100 occurrences, making learning rare but clinically important triplets questionable; no proposed solutions

Temporal modeling largely unexplored despite acknowledged importance; all evaluation appears frame-level rather than temporal sequence-level, unclear how much temporal boundary information helps versus frame-level labels
Small test set (5 videos only) with insufficient statistics: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or standard deviations reported for results

YOLO-Triplet baseline achieves worse performance than some YOLO variants (e.g., YOLOv11 superior on target branch at mAP@95: 48.84% vs 43.71%) while incurring significant computational cost (FPS: 77 vs 188), undermining the relational modeling contribution

strengths: Well-articulated motivation addressing three specific CholecT50 limitations with clinically-informed solutions
Rigorous multi-phase annotation with 50+ contributors including practicing surgeons, semi-automatic refinement, and mandatory triple review
Significantly higher task complexity with 38.93% frames containing 3+ concurrent instruments vs. 0% in CholecT50
Multi-institutional data integration (3 sources) with consistent re-annotation, addressing single-source bias
Comprehensive evaluation with multiple baselines clearly demonstrating weak vs. full supervision gap
Novel Triplet Perspective for tracking with principled justification over existing perspectives
Strong ethical practices including IRB approval, privacy protections, and thoughtful broader impact discussion
Dense spatial and temporal annotations with clinically-defined action boundaries
weaknesses: Weak absolute performance (36.02% mAP@50:95, 31.26% F1) acknowledged as below clinical deployment threshold, undermining practical applicability claims
Limited dataset scale (21 videos) with thin multi-institutional distribution (9 in-house, 8 PSI-AVA, 4 ESAD) constraining model learning capacity
No inter-annotator agreement quantification for bounding boxes or temporal boundaries despite being critical quality indicators
Proposed YOLO-Triplet baseline shows marginal improvements over YOLOv12 (36.02% vs. 34.08% mAP) with reduced efficiency (77.4 vs. 138.3 FPS), suggesting limited architectural insights
Long-tail distribution problem acknowledged but unresolved with no exploration of mitigation strategies or analysis of their impact
Temporal boundary definitions lack validation—2 second thresholds appear arbitrary without clinical validation or inter-rater agreement metrics
Missing ablation studies isolating contributions of bounding boxes, temporal definitions, and multi-institutional diversity
Incomplete tracking evaluation with brief section deferring details to supplementary and no empirical validation of Triplet Perspective
Limited generalizability evidence—only prostatectomy covered with weak justification for domain complexity claims
Potential demographic and institutional biases not addressed; generalization to lower-resource settings unclear

strengths: Addresses critical gap in existing datasets by providing first fully-supervised surgical triplet detection dataset with precise bounding box annotations and clinically-defined temporal boundaries
Rigorous annotation process with strong inter-rater agreement (Kappa=0.82), clinical supervision, and 60+ contributors including practicing surgeons
Comes with valuable practical contributions beyond the dataset: two novel open-source annotation tools (Triplet-labelme, SurgLabel) and enhanced evaluation toolkit (ivtdmetrics)
Multi-institutional composition (21 videos from 3 sources) increases credibility and reflects real-world surgical variability
Increased task complexity compared to CholecT50 (prostatectomy vs cholecystectomy with 58.77% frames having ≥3 concurrent instances vs 6.75%)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 14 methods benchmarked, 5-fold cross-validation, multiple protocols (frame-wise and video-wise), detailed per-class analysis
Strong reproducibility with detailed implementations, extensive appendices (32 pages), and clear data release plans
Baseline method (TDnet) demonstrates novel instance-level self-distillation approach for addressing class imbalance in surgical tasks
weaknesses: Limited to single surgical procedure (RARP only), reducing scope and generalizability compared to multi-procedure datasets; transferability of tools to other procedures unclear
Fewer unique procedures than prior work (21 videos vs 50 in CholecT50), which may limit model generalization across different surgeon styles and institutional practices
Severe class imbalance remains largely unresolved: baseline achieves only 36.1% mAP@0.5 for full triplets and 32.8% F1-score, suggesting task remains far from solved despite the dataset
Temporal information provided in annotations is not effectively utilized: Appendix G.2 shows temporal modules yielded 'limited results' and sometimes worse performance than frame-wise baselines

Low absolute performance metrics (34.7% precision, 39.7% recall, many high confusion rates) raise questions about practical clinical deployment feasibility without addressing error severity or clinical implications
Baseline method shows only marginal improvements over YOLOv12 (1.8% at mAP@0.5, 1.3% at mAP@0.5:0.95) despite added architectural complexity; limited algorithmic novelty
Inter-rater agreement validated on only 5 surgeons across 5 non-overlapping segments (1000 frames); no cross-annotator group comparison or temporal consistency analysis
Dataset composition is imbalanced across sources: PWH (41.3%), PSI-AVA (36.3%), ESAD (22.4%), potentially biasing models toward PWH characteristics with no stratification analysis
Re-annotation strategy discards existing annotations from ESAD and PSI-AVA rather than leveraging them, increasing effort but potentially introducing systematic biases; impact not analyzed

Incomplete baseline comparisons: weak-supervision methods perform at near-zero levels (not meaningful comparison), CholecQ dismissed without quantitative analysis, no cross-dataset transfer learning evaluation

strengths: Well-executed annotation with rigorous quality control (κ=0.82 inter-rater agreement), medical supervision, and 60+ contributors across multiple review cycles
Multi-institutional data from three sources with documented instrument variations, improving potential for generalization beyond single-center bias
Purpose-built annotation tools (Triplet-labelme and SurgLabel) with thoughtful affordances for surgical annotation efficiency (span-based batch labeling, adaptive track assignment)
Comprehensive benchmarking with 13 methods, detailed ablation studies, video-wise metrics, and per-class performance analysis
Clear clinical motivation for temporal boundary definitions that exceed CholecT50's ambiguity
Strong reproducibility commitment with promised release of code, dataset, tools, and detailed implementation specifications
weaknesses: Limited novelty: The dataset is largely CholecT50 + bounding boxes + different surgical procedure; switching procedures does not constitute a fundamental scientific contribution

Very poor absolute performance (36.1% mAP@IVT@0.5, 32.8% F1) raises serious questions about task formulation validity, yet authors provide no deep analysis of why the task is so hard or what this performance level means clinically
Severe class imbalance remains unsolved: Despite TDnet's distillation approach, 50+ rare categories still have AP<10%, and distillation provides only marginal gains (1.8% improvement over YOLOv12)

Unclear clinical relevance: Authors claim applications in surgical skill assessment and intraoperative guidance, but do not validate that 32.8% F1-score detection would enable these applications or provide measurable clinical outcomes

Temporal information fundamentally underexploited: Appendix G.2 admits temporal modeling provides minimal gains, suggesting per-frame detection is suboptimal; this core limitation should prompt rethinking the task, not deferral to future work
Limited true diversity: All 21 videos are robot-assisted prostatectomy; generalization to other procedures or technical variations is unknown, undermining multi-institutional claims

Confusing architectural choice for baseline: Ablation (Table 9) shows multi-task learning is the key factor, not self-distillation, suggesting TDnet is over-engineered; method appears post-hoc rather than methodologically motivated
No cross-dataset validation: Missing experiments comparing CholecT50-trained models on ProstaTD would substantiate claims of increased difficulty; comparisons are only within ProstaTD
High cross-validation variance: With only 21 videos (4-5 per test fold), standard deviations of ±1-5% indicate instability and suggest findings may not be robust

Annotation quality concerns: Semi-automatic initialization with cystoscopic model (domain mismatch) followed by 5 iterative correction cycles suggests initial predictions were poor; inter-rater agreement may not reflect absolute quality
Paper organization suggests weak core contributions: Extensive appendix (10+ pages), with important details scattered; tool contributions are engineering-focused rather than research advances

Missing critical analysis: Confusion matrix (Figure 9) shows frequent within-instrument action/target confusions, suggesting fundamental task decomposition issues that are noted but not adequately analyzed or addressed

strengths: Clear problem identification: Compelling articulation of three specific limitations in CholecT50 (no bounding boxes, unclear temporal boundaries, limited diversity)
High-quality dataset with rigorous annotation: 196,490 instances across 71,775 frames with strong inter-rater agreement (κ=0.82), conducted by 60+ contributors including practicing surgeons
Multi-institutional diversity: Data from 3 sources (PWH, PSI-AVA, ESAD) reflecting real-world variation in surgical practice and equipment
Practical community contributions beyond the dataset: Two generalizable annotation tools (Triplet-labelme and SurgLabel) and novel evaluation toolkit (ivtdmetrics) with lasting impact
Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation: 13 detection methods benchmarked with frame-wise and video-wise metrics, detailed ablations, and per-class analysis
Effective complexity analysis: Demonstrates ProstaTD's challenge (58.77% frames with ≥3 instances) vs CholecT50 (6.75%), justifying dataset value
Excellent presentation and reproducibility: Well-organized paper, extensive appendices, commitment to release code/data/tools, thorough implementation details
Clinically-informed design: Temporal boundaries defined by expert urologists with clear rules distinguishing continuous/momentary/null actions, reflecting real surgical practice
Open science commitment: Addresses ethical concerns with IRB approval, patient privacy protection, and thoughtful discussion of societal benefits/risks
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: TDnet applies straightforward combination of existing techniques (self-distillation + multi-task learning on YOLO); modest improvements over baselines (1.8% mAP gain)

Temporal modeling underutilized: Dismisses temporal approaches due to computational cost; lacks deeper investigation of why temporal information provides limited benefit despite its inherent importance in surgical videos

Absolute performance remains low for practical deployment: mAPIVT metrics (36.1%@0.5, 33.1%@0.5:0.95) and F1-score of 32.8% concerning for clinical use; many rare triplets show <10% AP with limited analysis of why
Dataset size and scope limitations: 21 surgical procedures modest for deep learning; no cross-dataset generalization evaluation (ProstaTD→CholecT50 or vice versa) to validate broader applicability

Incomplete annotation protocol analysis: Inter-rater study limited to 1,000 frames; arbitrary '2-second' threshold for continuous actions lacks justification; limited investigation of annotation disagreement patterns

Missing key ablations and analyses: No comparison of CholecT50-based methods retrained on ProstaTD; absent statistical significance testing; confusion matrix analysis lacks systematic exploration of error sources
Insufficient investigation of class imbalance problem: Despite TDnet's focus on imbalance mitigation, low performance on rare triplets persists; limited guidance for practitioners handling rare cases
Generalization concerns: Dataset limited to prostatectomy; tools tested only on this procedure; unclear transferability to other surgical domains or patient populations

Potential reproducibility gaps: Dataset access mechanism not fully specified ('at [link]' not visible); anonymization methodology vaguely described; legal enforceability of commercial-use restrictions unclear
